pull_request.title: feat: implement signature_verification_in_loop lint
pull_request.body:
Closes #47

## Summary

Adds a lint that flags `env.crypto().ed25519_verify(...)`, `env.crypto().secp256k1_recover(...)`, and `env.crypto().secp256r1_verify(...)` calls made inside a loop body (`for`, `while`, or `loop`).

Elliptic-curve signature verification is one of the most CPU-expensive host functions a Soroban contract can call. Unlike a host call whose result is constant across iterations (already covered by [`unnecessary_host_function_call`](docs/lints/unnecessary_host_function_call.md)), this cost can't be hoisted out of the loop — each iteration is genuinely verifying a *different* signature. Verifying signatures one at a time in a loop is almost always a structural sign that the contract should use a signature scheme that supports batch/aggregate verification, or should move per-item authorization to a bulk entrypoint instead.

## Implementation details

- `SignatureVerificationInLoop` is a `check_expr` pass matching a fixed method-name list (`SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION_METHODS`: `ed25519_verify`, `secp256k1_recover`, `secp256r1_verify`) on a receiver whose type (via `cx.typeck_results()`) is `soroban_sdk::crypto::Crypto` or `soroban_sdk::crypto::CryptoHazmat`.
- Reuses the existing `enclosing_loop` helper (same one `contract_call_in_loop`/`soroban_storage_in_loop` use) rather than `enclosing_loop_or_closure`, matching the more conservative "syntactic loop only" behavior of the other unconditional-cost lints.
- **Unlike `unnecessary_host_function_call`, this lint does *not* check `depends_on_loop_state`.** The cost here is inherent to what the loop is doing (verifying N different signatures costs N verifications no matter what), so it's structurally identical in spirit to `contract_call_in_loop`, which also flags every loop-body call unconditionally rather than only "wasted, invariant" ones.
- Scope is deliberately limited to these three well-established, unambiguous primitives for a first pass. `Address::require_auth()`/`require_auth_for_args()` (Soroban's higher-level auth framework) and the BLS12-381/BN254 pairing-check APIs are documented as out of scope in the lint page — the former has a distinct cost profile tracked as its own proposal, and the latter are general-purpose curve operations rather than a single named "verify" call, so reliably recognizing a signature-verification *usage* of them needs more context than a fixed method-name match.

## Files

**New:**
- `docs/lints/signature_verification_in_loop.md` — lint reference page.

**Modified:**
- `soroban_cost_lints/src/lib.rs` — `SignatureVerificationInLoop` late lint pass, `SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION_METHODS` constant, `LINT_METADATA`/`register_lints` wiring (category: `Compute`).
- `soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.rs` / `ui/main.stderr` — new UI fixtures (see Tests below); the mock `Crypto` struct in the test harness gained `ed25519_verify`/`secp256k1_recover`/`secp256r1_verify` stubs alongside its existing `sha256`/`keccak256`.
- `README.md`, `docs/lints/README.md`, `docs/cost_rationale.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — lint listed under CPU/Compute with rationale and target-resource summary.

**Test files:** all under `soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.rs` (fixtures) / `soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.stderr` (expected diagnostics), following this repo's existing UI-test convention.

## Tests added

All in the new `signature_verification_in_loop — Fixtures` section of `ui/main.rs`:

- `bad_ed25519_verify_in_for_loop` — `ed25519_verify` in a `for` loop → **warns**.
- `bad_secp256k1_recover_in_while_loop` — `secp256k1_recover` in a `while` loop → **warns**.
- `bad_secp256r1_verify_in_loop_loop` — `secp256r1_verify` in a `loop` → **warns**.
- `good_ed25519_verify_outside_loop` — single call, not in a loop → no warning.
- `allowed_ed25519_verify_in_loop` — same loop case suppressed via `#[allow(signature_verification_in_loop)]` → no warning.

## How to test

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
```

All three pass locally. The UI test (`cargo test -p soroban_cost_lints`) exercises the new fixtures against the bundled `ui/main.stderr` expectations.

commits.message:
feat: implement signature_verification_in_loop lint

Flag env.crypto().ed25519_verify(...), secp256k1_recover(...), and
secp256r1_verify(...) calls made inside a loop body. Elliptic-curve
signature verification is one of the most CPU-expensive host functions
available, and unlike a host call with a constant result, this cost
cannot be hoisted out of the loop: each iteration verifies a different
signature. Verifying signatures one at a time in a loop is a structural
sign that the contract should use a scheme that supports batch or
aggregate verification, or move per-item auth to a bulk callee
entrypoint.

- Add SignatureVerificationInLoop late lint pass matching the three
  Crypto/CryptoHazmat signature-verification and key-recovery methods,
  unconditionally flagged inside a loop (no loop-invariance check, since
  the cost is inherent to what the loop is doing, matching the existing
  contract_call_in_loop lint's approach).
- Add UI fixtures covering all three methods across for/while/loop forms,
  a call outside a loop, and an #[allow] suppression case.
- Document the lint in docs/lints/signature_verification_in_loop.md, the
  README feature list, docs/lints/README.md, docs/cost_rationale.md, and
  CHANGELOG.md, including why Address::require_auth() and BLS/BN254
  pairing checks are deliberately out of scope for this first pass.

Closes #47

Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/main' into feat/signature-verification-in-loop

# Conflicts:
#	soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.stderr

fix: resolve CI build failures in SARIF output and fixture workspace

- SarifRun.results was typed Vec<SarifResult> while the SARIF result
  builder constructed plain serde_json::Value objects via json!(),
  a leftover mismatch from a prior merge that broke compilation.
  Retype results as Vec<serde_json::Value>, drop the now-dead typed
  Sarif* structs, and wire the already-collected rule descriptors
  into tool.driver.rules.
- integration.rs used HashSet<String> but inserted &str literals;
  fix the declared type.
- alpha/beta fixture crates each declared their own [workspace]
  while also being listed as members of the parent workspace,
  causing cargo metadata to fail with "multiple workspace roots
  found". Drop the redundant per-crate [workspace] tables.

These were the actual cause of the "SARIF result missing level"
CI failures reported on PRs #232, #267, #269, #270 (all inherited
the same broken merge state) — the binary failed to compile, it
was not a runtime field-mapping bug.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
